questions.prompt: Why do immutable container images make rollbacks reliable?

options.text: Because you patch the running server in place
Because rolling back just means running the previous image (by digest); nothing is modified in place
Because rollbacks require rebuilding from source

questions.explanation: Each version is an immutable image, so a deploy is 'run the new image' and a rollback is 'run the previous one' — both are simple and repeatable.

questions.prompt: What is the main drawback of the recreate strategy?

options.text: There is downtime between stopping the old version and starting the new one
It runs three versions at once

questions.explanation: Recreate stops the old version before starting the new one, so there is a gap with downtime. It is simple and fine when brief downtime is acceptable.

questions.prompt: What must you be careful about during a rolling update?

options.text: Both versions run at the same time, so they must be compatible (especially with a shared database)

questions.explanation: A rolling update replaces instances gradually, so old and new versions coexist for a while and must be compatible, particularly around database schema changes.

questions.prompt: Releasing a new version to a small percentage of users first, then expanding based on metrics, is called a ______ deployment. (one word)
questions.explanation: A canary deployment limits the blast radius by exposing the new version to a small fraction of traffic before ramping up.

questions.prompt: How does blue-green deployment enable near-instant rollback?

options.text: By deleting the old version immediately
By keeping the old (blue) environment running and switching traffic back to it if the new (green) one misbehaves

questions.explanation: Blue-green keeps both environments; traffic is switched to green, but blue stays ready so you can switch back instantly if needed.

questions.prompt: Match each deployment strategy to its defining trait.

pairs.right: Stop old, then start new (brief downtime)
Two environments; switch traffic all at once
Small percentage first, expand on good metrics

questions.explanation: Each strategy trades off downtime, resource usage, and rollback speed differently; choose based on the change's risk.
